convoLines.text: "I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
"My theory changes weekly. This week's: we're the control group. Somewhere there's a village that got instructions, and we're the ones they just... watched. Cheerful thought, right?"
"Still on what you think happened to us."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Chorus Line? I'm pushing 'Big Ugly'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Isabella shifts their weight. "I need something to do. Anything. Please."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Isabella shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone?"
"I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
Something in them stays shut, for now.
"Still on needing to be alone."
"With you leading? ...Give me a day to think."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Have you heard what they're calling Chorus Line? Alejandro is pushing 'Big Ugly'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Mayapple — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Alejandro. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'Alright — carefully, now. Both of us.'"
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Isabella digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1947 kcal to the pantry.)
"Sleep's gone strange. I sleep in short shifts at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Nobody says Penelope's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Do you dream about before? Or is it all — this — now?"
"Then it's not gone. Not really. Keep going back."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"If this is about feelings, I'm charging by the minute."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Siege. They just... took Kahukura. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"My part? I braid grass while listening to plans and stay ready."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Alejandro grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Alejandro is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I tried the Mayapple like you showed me. Didn't poison anyone, so that's a win."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson. I mean it."
The moment passes without landing. Not yet.
"Go ahead — you've got my attention."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Kahukura — Siege, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Alejandro nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"I don't keep score on that. Score-keeping is how you stop sleeping. I do what the day needs and I don't rehearse it after."
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "They say the table's coming. For us. I keep thinking about what we'd even bring to it."
"I keep my eyes down when I pass it. Respect, maybe. Fear, probably. Both."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Isabella nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Whatever door it is — it'll still be there tomorrow. That's the worst part. The patience."
You show them Mayapple — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You take those walks that don't need to happen. Still breathing your own air?"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
It's quiet at the hollow. Isabella doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff. Anyway, that's me."
A beat. Then, as if shaking something off:
"Right — go on, I'm listening."
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.

Kahukura nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)

"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."

"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."

"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
"Sure — Anger's a fire — useful if you cook with it, deadly if you sleep next to it. I cook with mine. Most days."
"Still on whether you're angry."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They say the table's coming. For us. I keep thinking about what we'd even bring to it."

"About that question — What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on what you did for fun."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I keep turning it over and there's nothing new in it."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"

Alejandro nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)

"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"You said you dream about before. Every night — the only place it still exists. Is it still there?"

"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."

lines: d40: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Penelope Fisher is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d40: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d40: 🕯️ Penelope is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d40: Thornfield watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d40: 🕯️ Penelope Fisher is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d40: What Penelope kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d40: "Penelope's gone." Alejandro looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Penelope." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d40: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. James blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Camp Cooking (Level 1). Cooking uses half the water, +10% kcal. Once per day: add a Secret Ingredient (a random inventory item) — 50% delicious (+morale), 50% educational.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d40: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d40: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d40: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d40: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Penelope Fisher, 40 days. The mantle passes to James Palmer.
d40: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. James Palmer, 29 — a Baker. His hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Lucky Rock.
d40: The village's quarrel was with Penelope — and Penelope is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d40: At the grave, Alejandro, Isabella, Kahukura and 5 more speak for James — "Penelope trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d40: The fire knew James before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d111: — DAY 111 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d111: Overnight, 7 Groundnut went bad — beyond saving. You leave it for the flies.
d111: Fresh food keeps days, not weeks. Smoke it over a fire to make it last.
d111: The fire burns low. One new line in the journal: Hickory Nuts — named and noted.
d111: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. Your sleeping body burned less — 39 kcal conserved. By the fire. Good enough.)
